title: Dans l'ascenseur avec Hippolyte  (In the Elevator with Hippolyte)

segments.t: Inside the ASK elevator, Mathias shares an uncomfortable private conversation with his son Hippolyte. They discuss Catherine's depression and Hippolyte's new relationship, before Camille greets Mathias in the lobby. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Comment va ta mère?
Le bromazépam est devenu son meilleur ami.
C'est toujours très gênant.
En tout cas tu es là.
J'ai besoin de prendre un peu de recul.
Je passe beaucoup de temps chez ma copine.
Tu as une copine?
Oui, c'est tout récent.
Bon, je vais y aller.
On s'appelle? Bien sûr.
Au revoir... Merde pour ce soir!
Pardon, excusez-moi, Mathias.
Je vous passe votre prochain appel.
Let's examine how Mathias and Hippolyte share a quiet family moment step by step.
Comment va ta mère?
'How is your mother?' Mathias gently asks about Catherine's mental state after their separation.
Le bromazépam est devenu son meilleur ami.
'Bromazepam has become her best friend.' Hippolyte describes his mother's heavy reliance on tranquilizers.
C'est toujours très gênant.
'It is always very awkward.' Hippolyte opens with the word for 'is' and lands on 'awkward.' at the close.
En tout cas tu es là.
'In any case you are here.' Listen for the expression meaning 'case', which leads naturally into 'here.'.
J'ai besoin de prendre un peu de recul.
'I need to get some distance.' The key word here means 'I have', paired with 'distance.' to make the point clear.
Je passe beaucoup de temps chez ma copine.
'I spend a lot of time at my girlfriend\'s place.' Hippolyte explains why he has been avoiding the family apartment.
Tu as une copine?
'You have a girlfriend?' Mathias is surprised by this unexpected news about his son's personal life.
Oui, c'est tout récent.
'Yes, it is very recent.' Hippolyte opens with the word for 'yes' and lands on 'recent.' at the close.
Bon, je vais y aller.
'Well, I will get going.' Hippolyte prepares to exit as the elevator arrives at the lobby.
On s'appelle? Bien sûr.
'We will call each other? Of course.' Father and son promise to stay in touch by telephone.
Au revoir... Merde pour ce soir!
'Goodbye... Good luck for tonight!' The key word here means 'seeing again...', paired with 'evening!' to make the point clear.
Pardon, excusez-moi, Mathias.
'Pardon, excuse me, Mathias.' Camille politely interrupts her father in the corridor.
Je vous passe votre prochain appel.
'I am putting through your next call.' Notice how the verb for 'put through' leads straight into 'call.'. Now let's listen to the conversation in the elevator once more.

Hippolyte leaves to meet his girlfriend, wishing his father good luck for the evening. Back in Gabriel's office, Sofia is furious after an explosive argument with casting director Constance. See you in the next scene.
